Relative stability of the gas-phase conformers can be estimated from intramolecular H-bonding and steric strain. A shorter donor-acceptor O···O separation with a H···O ~1.9–2.3 Å signals a stabilising O–H···O contact, while long O···O separations and/or eclipsed backbone segments are destabilising. Conformers where the donor finds O9 as the better acceptor, e.g. 2, 7, 4, 21, 26, still show the same trend and are placed by their minimal O···O distance. Conformers with O···O > ~3.0 Å show little or no H-bond and lie progressively lower. The ordering among the very top 5–8 conformers is sensitive to sub-Å distance errors and to local steric contacts that cannot be fully resolved from coordinates alone; the overall trend from short, H-bonded, extended structures to long, non-H-bonded, more folded structures is robust.
